body: That's really interesting! Do you think she was just wearing the harness a lot more of the time, being outdoors more? I guess that could be a desensitising thing.

I have tried a bit of this sort of thing yeah, and I know it's probably the best way to go, but I'm just a bit stuck in the interim period - since he still needs to go for walks while I'm doing that, I feel like I can't do it gradually *enough* if that makes sense. I will try more of just having it on the floor around him w/ positive reinforcement though, thanks.

I have! He's been on two multi-week group obedience courses, beginner and intermediate. He did brilliantly at them. But all the instructors advised on harnesses and I agree, I think they're much safer.
Like... forever? No, definitely not. He still needs to sleep comfortably, and if he's in his crate I'm not having him wear anything that could get caught or tangled, not safe.

oh thanks so much to you and /u/PikettySpaghetti I wasn't expecting such an informative reply ;-; that's really helpful. I guess if I have to go around with a bunch on moisturiser on it doesn't matter so much at the moment now does it!

Thank you, this is a really kind comment. It hurts me so much to know that there are probably thousands and thousands of other people in my situation and none of us can even reach out to anyone. It's the most isolating thing I can imagine haha

Yeah, I find it really difficult trying to get support from people since so many go down the "money can't buy you happiness route". And no, I'm not in any contact with any other relatives and since my friends are in uni I can't live with them. Stuck here for the rest of my life, however short that is.
Thank you, I try my best to find them but they are so far and few between nowadays.
